newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea's Supreme Court set to rule on Roh, Chun.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea's Supreme Court set to rule on Roh, Chun.

text.p: South Korea's Supreme Court is set to rule on a demand by state prosecutors for harsher penalties for former presidents Chun Doo Hwan and Roh Tae-woo, a court official said on Monday.
Prosecutors challenged as too lenient an appeal court's decision last December to commute Chun's death sentence to life in jail and to cut to 17 years Roh's 22-1/2 year prison term.
The ruling by the Supreme Court -- South Korea's court of final appeal -- will be made on April 17, the official said.

Chun and Roh were found guilty of mutiny and treason in connection with a 1979 coup that launched Chun's rise to power and a 1980 massacre of pro-democracy activists in the southwestern city of Kwangju.
The disgraced former heads of state were also convicted of corruption after amassing huge slush funds.
Chun was president from 1980-88 and Roh succeeded him, stepping down in 1993.
Prosecutors also challenged acquittals of two businessmen, Hanbo Group chairman Chung Tae-soo and the former president of Daewoo Corp Lee Kyung-hoon.
Separately, Daewoo Group chairman Kim Woo-choong and Dong-Ah Group chairman Choi won-suk are appealing against their suspended prison terms. All the tycoons were originally convicted of bribery.
The Supreme Court is also reviewing cases involving 14 ex-generals, convicted of mutiny and sedition, and four one-time presidential aides, found guilty of corruption.
One of the generals died last week.
Hanbo founder Chung is now standing trial on bribery and other charges in connection with the collapse of his group's flagship steelmaker in January.
